epic_n_new_lyme.long_name: Patients with a New Lyme Disease Diagnosis
epic_n_new_lyme.short_description: Monthly count of patients with a new Lyme disease diagnosis.
epic_n_new_lyme.long_description: Monthly count of patients with a new Lyme disease diagnosis, per Epic's new-case measure ("n new ..."; first-time diagnoses only, excluding patients already diagnosed before the month). Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed by Epic (reported blank or as "10 or fewer") and imputed as 5; see epic_new_lyme_suppressed_flag.
epic_n_new_lyme.statement: In {location}, {value} patients had a new Lyme disease diagnosis.

epic_pct_new_lyme.long_name: Percent of Patients with a New Lyme Disease Diagnosis
epic_pct_new_lyme.short_description: Monthly percent of patients with a new Lyme disease diagnosis.
epic_pct_new_lyme.long_description: Monthly percentage of patients with a new Lyme disease diagnosis, computed as epic_n_new_lyme / epic_n_patients * 100 - a percent of all patients, not a rate per 100,000. Where the numerator was suppressed it is imputed as 5 before the percentage is computed. Where the denominator was itself suppressed the percentage is left missing, because dividing by the imputed denominator of 5 would assert a meaningless value; those cells are marked by epic_n_patients_suppressed_flag.
epic_pct_new_lyme.statement: In {location}, {value}% of patients had a new Lyme disease diagnosis.

epic_new_lyme_suppressed_flag.long_name: Suppression flag for the Lyme disease new-case numerator (count and percent)
epic_new_lyme_suppressed_flag.short_description: Indicates whether the Lyme disease new-case numerator was suppressed and imputed; applies to both epic_n_new_lyme and epic_pct_new_lyme.
epic_new_lyme_suppressed_flag.long_description: 1 when Epic Cosmos suppressed the Lyme disease cell (a count of 10 or fewer, reported blank or as "10 or fewer") and epic_n_new_lyme was imputed as 5; 0 otherwise. Suppression of the denominator is tracked separately by epic_n_patients_suppressed_flag.

epic_n_patients.short_description: Monthly total patient count, used as the denominator for each disease's percentage.
epic_n_patients.long_description: Monthly total count of patients, used as the denominator for each epic_pct_new_* column. Data from Epic Cosmos SlicerDicer session 2861722. Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed by Epic and imputed as 5; see epic_n_patients_suppressed_flag. Population base: All Patients, Country of Care = United States of America, Has Any Encounters. Same denominator definition as cosmos_vector_borne.

epic_n_patients_suppressed_flag.long_name: Suppression flag for the total patient count
epic_n_patients_suppressed_flag.short_description: Indicates whether the total patient count was suppressed and imputed.
epic_n_patients_suppressed_flag.long_description: 1 when Epic Cosmos suppressed the denominator cell (a count of 10 or fewer, reported blank or as "10 or fewer") and epic_n_patients was imputed as 5; 0 otherwise. Where this flag is 1, every epic_pct_new_* column is left missing rather than computed from an imputed denominator.

epic_cosmos.name: Epic Cosmos
epic_cosmos.description: Epic Cosmos is a collaborative research platform containing de-identified patient data from over 300 million patients across more than 1,600 hospitals and health systems using Epic electronic health record systems. Data is accessed via SlicerDicer, a self-service analytics tool. The dataset includes emergency department visits, diagnoses, immunizations, laboratory results, and other clinical data. Due to privacy protections, counts fewer than 10 are suppressed and imputed. Coverage extends across all U.S. states and territories. Note that county-level and city-level stratifications could differ markedly in total sample size due to high levels of missingness of county data in some states.
epic_cosmos.restrictions: The data can be re-used with appropriate attribution. A suggested citation relating to this data is 'Results of research performed with Epic Cosmos were obtained from the PopHIVE platform (https://github.com/PopHIVE/Ingest).'
